Ives argues the board reversed course because losing Nvidia's founder at the start of the Rubin AI chip cycle posed a greater risk to shareholders than bringing him back. He sees a potential path toward a $300 valuation target, but only after outstanding governance, national security and export-control investigations are resolved.
